1.title: CRACK THE STEWARDSHIP CODE

scripture.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

1.truth:
Money must never become the master of our hearts. God gives us money as a tool to manage,
deploy and use for His purposes.

points.title: Everyone Serves a Master
points.body:
Jesus did not say that having money is wrong. He warned that serving money is wrong.

A master is anything that controls your choices, commands your loyalty and determines your
priorities.

Money becomes a master when:

- You disobey God to obtain it.
- You lie to keep it.
- You measure your worth by it.
- You cannot release it when God directs you to give.
- You place financial gain above righteousness.

The first question in stewardship is not, “How much money do I have?”

It is, “Who rules my heart?”

points.title: Money Was Created to Serve
points.body:
Money can be used to:

- Buy food.
- Pay school fees.
- Support families.
- Build businesses.
- Spread the gospel.
- Educate children.
- Solve community problems.
- Create opportunities.

Money is powerful, but it must remain in its proper position.

It must remain in your hand and never sit on the throne of your heart.

points.title: Stewardship Is Management Under God
points.body:
A steward is not the final owner. A steward manages what belongs to someone else.

God owns everything, but He entrusts different portions of His resources to different
people.

He expects us to manage those resources:

- Faithfully
- Wisely
- Honestly
- Productively
- Generously
- Eternally

supporting.text: The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.
And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

1.illustration:
Imagine a powerful car without a driver.

The car may have speed, strength and value, but without someone controlling it, it can cause
destruction.

Money is like that car.

It can take you forward when properly directed, but it can destroy lives when it is allowed
to control the driver.

You must remain in the driver’s seat under the direction of Jesus Christ.
1.challenge:
Write down your honest answers to these three questions:

- What do I currently believe money can do for me?
- What financial pressure most easily controls my emotions?
- How can I begin making money serve God’s purpose?
1.prayer:
Father, teach me the secrets of faithful stewardship. Deliver my heart from greed, fear,
comparison and the love of money. Let Jesus Christ remain my Master, and teach me to make
money a useful servant. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
1.declaration:
Jesus Christ is my Master.
Money is my servant.
I will learn and live the Stewardship Code.
1.transition: Before we can learn how to manage money, we must first settle the question of ownership.

2.title: THE OWNER

scripture.text: The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

2.truth:
Everything belongs to God. Stewardship begins when we stop acting like absolute owners and
begin living as responsible managers.

points.title: God Owns the World
points.body:
The earth did not create itself, and we did not bring ourselves into existence.

God created:

- The land
- The oceans
- The minerals
- The plants
- The animals
- Human intelligence
- Human strength
- Every opportunity for productivity

Therefore, God is not merely one participant in the economy. He is the ultimate Owner of
everything within it.

points.title: God Owns What Is in Your Hands
points.body:
Your phone may have your name on it. Your parents may have purchased it. But the materials,
intelligence, health and opportunity that made the purchase possible came from God.

God owns:

- Your time
- Your abilities
- Your education
- Your possessions
- Your opportunities
- Your future
- Your influence

You are responsible for how these resources are used.

points.title: Ownership Changes Behaviour
points.body:
When you understand that something belongs to God, you treat it differently.

You will be less likely to:

- Waste it.
- Destroy it.
- Use it for sin.
- Neglect it.
- Compare it carelessly.
- Take it for granted.

The awareness of God’s ownership creates responsibility.

supporting.text: The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, saith the LORD of hosts.

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty: for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is thine; thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and thou art exalted as head above all.

2.illustration:
Suppose a friend lends you an expensive laptop for a week.

Because the laptop belongs to someone else, you would probably:

- Carry it carefully.
- Keep food and water away from it.
- Avoid dangerous downloads.
- Return it on time.
- Report any problem immediately.

You would treat it carefully because you know you are accountable to the owner.

Your life and resources should be treated with even greater care because they belong to God.
2.challenge:
Create a list titled:

#### “What God Owns but Has Placed in My Hands”

Include at least seven things, such as time, money, devices, skills and opportunities.
2.prayer:
Father, open my eyes to see that everything belongs to You. Deliver me from wastefulness and
entitlement. Help me manage every resource as something entrusted to me by You. In Jesus’
name. Amen.
2.declaration:
God owns everything.
Everything in my hands belongs to Him.
2.transition: If God is the Owner, what does that make us?

3.title: THE STEWARD

scripture.text: And he said also unto his disciples, There was a certain rich man, which had a steward; and the same was accused unto him that he had wasted his goods.

3.truth: A steward manages another person’s resources according to the owner’s instructions.

points.title: A Steward Is a Manager
points.body:
The steward in Luke 16 was responsible for the rich man’s property.

He did not own the resources, but he had:

- Access
- Authority
- Opportunity
- Responsibility

Being a steward means God allows us to handle resources that still belong to Him.

points.title: Access Is Not Ownership
points.body:
Having access to something does not mean you can use it carelessly.

You may have access to:

- Your parents’ money
- A family car
- School equipment
- Church property
- Internet access
- A leadership position
- Another person’s trust

Access creates responsibility. It does not remove accountability.

points.title: A Steward Must Be Faithful
points.body:
The most important quality of a steward is not popularity, intelligence or wealth.

It is faithfulness.

Faithfulness means:

- Doing what is right consistently.
- Protecting what has been entrusted.
- Following instructions.
- Producing the expected result.
- Remaining honest when nobody is watching.

supporting.text: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
As every man hath received the gift, even so minister the same one to another, as good stewards of the manifold grace of God.

3.illustration:
A school prefect has authority, but the prefect does not own the school.

The prefect cannot invent personal rules merely to impress friends. The authority was given
to serve the school’s purpose.

In the same way, God gives us resources and influence to serve His purposes, not merely to
please ourselves.
3.challenge:
Choose one resource from yesterday’s inventory and answer:

- Why has God placed this in my hands?
- Who can it help?
- How can I manage it better?
3.prayer:
Lord, make me a faithful steward. Help me use every privilege, possession and opportunity
according to Your purpose. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
3.declaration:
I am not the ultimate owner.
I am God’s faithful steward.
3.transition:
A steward must know not only who owns the resources but also where those resources came
from.

4.title: THE SOURCE

scripture.text: But thou shalt remember the LORD thy God: for it is he that giveth thee power to get wealth, that he may establish his covenant which he sware unto thy fathers, as it is this day.

4.truth:
God is the Source. Money, jobs, businesses and opportunities are channels through which His
provision may come.

points.title: God Gives the Power to Produce
points.body:
Money does not normally fall from heaven.

It may come through:

- Work
- Business
- Creativity
- Skill
- Investment
- Gifts
- Opportunities

But behind every legitimate channel is the God who gives:

- Life
- Health
- Intelligence
- Strength
- Favour
- Ideas
- Relationships
- Opportunity

Never worship the channel and forget the Source.

points.title: The Source Is Greater Than the Resource
points.body:
A resource can finish.

A job may end. A customer may leave. A gift may be spent. An opportunity may change.

But God remains.

When your trust is in God, you can remain peaceful even when one channel of provision
changes.

points.title: Remembering God Produces Humility
points.body:
Success can make people say:

- “I did it all by myself.”
- “Nobody helped me.”
- “I do not need anyone.”
- “My intelligence gave me everything.”

The Bible tells us to remember the Lord because remembrance protects us from pride.

supporting.text: Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning.
But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort? for all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

4.illustration:
A child receives ₦5,000 from a parent and uses ₦500 to buy the parent a birthday gift.

The gift is meaningful, but the money originally came from the parent.

In the same way, everything we offer to God first came from Him.
4.challenge:
Write down three channels through which God currently provides for you.

Beside each one, write:

“God is my Source; this is only a channel.”
4.prayer:
Father, help me remember You in every season of success. Keep me humble and grateful. Let my
confidence remain in You and not merely in money or people. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
4.declaration:
God is my Source.
Money is only a resource.
4.transition: If God gives us resources, then those resources must carry an assignment.

5.title: THE ASSIGNMENT

scripture.text: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

5.truth:
Every resource God gives carries an assignment. We must discover what it was given to
accomplish.

points.title: God Gives Resources for a Reason
points.body:
The master did not give the servants money merely to admire or display.

He expected them to use it productively.

God gives resources so they can:

- Meet needs
- Build capacity
- Create value
- Bless people
- Support families
- Advance His Kingdom
- Produce a responsible increase

points.title: Every Resource Has Potential
points.body:
A phone can become:

- A distraction
- A classroom
- A camera
- A business tool
- A Bible
- A design studio
- A communication platform

The object may be the same, but the assignment determines how it is used.

points.title: Ask Purpose Before Pleasure
points.body:
Before using a resource, ask:

- Why did God allow me to have this?
- What good can it accomplish?
- What problem can it solve?
- Who can it help?
- How can it honour God?

Pleasure is not automatically sinful, but purpose must lead pleasure.

supporting.text: For we are his workmanship, created in Christ Jesus unto good works, which God hath before ordained that we should walk in them.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

5.illustration:
Two teenagers receive identical smartphones.

One uses the phone mainly for endless scrolling and entertainment.

The other learns video editing, designs flyers, studies courses and helps a church media
team.

The difference is not the device. The difference is purpose.
5.challenge: Select one resource you own and write three productive assignments it can fulfil.
5.prayer:
Lord, show me the purpose of everything You have placed in my hands. Deliver me from using
valuable resources only for temporary pleasure. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
5.declaration:
Everything God gives me has an assignment.
I will use it for His purpose.
5.transition: Because every resource has an assignment, every steward must eventually give a report.

6.title: THE ACCOUNT

scripture.text: And he called him, and said unto him, How is it that I hear this of thee? give an account of thy stewardship; for thou mayest be no longer steward.

6.truth: Every steward will eventually explain what was done with what was received.

points.title: God Keeps Records
points.body:
The steward’s management was reviewed.

In the same way, God sees:

- How we use our time
- How we handle money
- How we treat people
- How we develop our abilities
- How we respond to opportunities
- How we use our influence

Nothing entrusted to us is outside His concern.

points.title: Accountability Improves Responsibility
points.body:
Knowing that an assignment will be graded changes how a serious student approaches it.

In the same way, knowing that we will give an account should help us:

- Plan better
- Waste less
- Obey faster
- Work diligently
- Remain honest
- Live intentionally

points.title: Accountability Is Personal
points.body:
Each person must answer for his or her own stewardship.

You cannot blame:

- Your friends
- Your parents
- Your school
- Your siblings
- Social media
- Your background

These things may influence you, but you must still make responsible choices.

supporting.text: So then every one of us shall give account of himself to God.
For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ; that every one may receive the things done in his body, according to that he hath done, whether it be good or bad.

6.illustration:
A student who knows there will be an examination does not wait until the examiner enters the
room before beginning to learn.

The coming examination influences today’s preparation.

Eternal accountability should influence today’s stewardship.
6.challenge:
Review how you used the following during the past seven days:

- Time
- Money
- Internet access
- Talents
- Opportunities

Write one improvement beside each area.
6.prayer:
Father, help me live with accountability. Give me wisdom to manage today in a way that will
please You when I give my report. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
6.declaration: I will manage today because I will report tomorrow.
6.transition: Tomorrow, we will gather the lessons of the Ownership Code into a personal covenant.

7.title: THE OWNERSHIP COVENANT

scripture.text: But who am I, and what is my people, that we should be able to offer so willingly after this sort? for all things come of thee, and of thine own have we given thee.

7.truth: Everything belongs to God, and everything in our hands must be managed as a sacred trust.

points.title: God Is the Owner
points.body:
This week, we learned that God owns:

- The world
- Silver and gold
- Our abilities
- Our opportunities
- Our time
- Our lives

God is not asking to become part-owner. He already owns everything.

points.title: I Am the Steward
points.body:
A steward receives:

- Resources
- Responsibility
- Instructions
- Opportunity

A steward must respond with faithfulness.

The question is not merely, “What do I have?”

The better question is, “How am I managing what belongs to God?”

points.title: My Life Is an Assignment
points.body:
Your life is not an accident.

Your abilities, environment, relationships and opportunities can become tools through which
God’s purpose is fulfilled.

Stewardship means turning what God has given you into service, value and impact.

supporting.text: Moreover it is required in stewards, that a man be found faithful.
The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein.

7.illustration:
A trusted courier may carry a package worth millions of naira.

The package may be in the courier’s hands, but it does not belong to the courier.

The courier’s success is measured by whether the package reaches the right destination in
the right condition.

Your success as a steward is measured by whether God’s resources fulfil God’s assignment
through your life.
7.challenge:
Your life is not an accident.

Your abilities, environment, relationships and opportunities can become tools through which
God’s purpose is fulfilled.

Stewardship means turning what God has given you into service, value and impact.
7.prayer:
Father, I acknowledge You as the Owner of my life and everything connected to me. Make me a
faithful steward. Let every resource in my hands fulfil Your purpose. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

8.title: FAITHFUL IN LITTLE

scripture.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

8.truth:
Little resources are not meaningless. They are tests that reveal whether we are ready for
greater responsibility.

points.title: Little Reveals Character
points.body:
Many people say:

- “I will save when I earn more.”
- “I will give when I become rich.”
- “I will become responsible when I have a business.”
- “I will stop wasting money when I receive more.”

Jesus teaches that behaviour in little predicts behaviour in much.

points.title: More Does Not Repair Bad Habits
points.body:
If a person wastes ₦1,000, the same person may waste ₦100,000.

A larger income does not automatically create:

- Discipline
- Wisdom
- Integrity
- Contentment
- Generosity

These qualities must be developed before increase arrives.

points.title: Little Is Training
points.body:
Small amounts teach you how to:

- Record
- Budget
- Save
- Give
- Delay gratification
- Make choices
- Resist pressure

Do not despise the training ground.

supporting.text: For who hath despised the day of small things? for they shall rejoice, and shall see the plummet in the hand of Zerubbabel with those seven; they are the eyes of the LORD, which run to and fro through the whole earth.
His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

8.illustration:
A leaking bucket does not first need more water.

It needs the leak repaired.

Pouring more water into a leaking bucket only creates a larger waste.

Before asking God for more, identify and repair the leaks in your present stewardship.
8.challenge:
Identify three small resources you currently manage.

For each one, write one habit that would demonstrate faithfulness.
8.prayer:
Father, help me become faithful in little. Teach me not to despise small beginnings or delay
discipline until increase comes. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
8.declaration:
My little is not useless.
My little is my test.
8.transition: To manage faithfully, you must first know what you have and where it is going.

9.title: KNOW WHAT YOU HAVE

scripture.text: Be thou diligent to know the state of thy flocks, and look well to thy herds.

9.truth: You cannot manage accurately what you refuse to measure.

points.title: Good Stewards Pay Attention
points.body:
In Bible times, flocks and herds represented wealth.

The owner had to know:

- How many animals were present
- Which ones were healthy
- Which ones were missing
- Which ones were growing
- Which ones required attention

Modern stewardship also requires awareness.

points.title: Records Reveal Reality
points.body:
You may feel that you do not spend much, but written records may reveal otherwise.

Keeping records helps you see:

- Repeated purchases
- Wasteful habits
- Emotional spending
- Forgotten debts
- Missed savings
- Giving patterns

Facts help you make better decisions.

points.title: Measure More Than Money
points.body:
Teenagers should also track:

- Time
- Internet use
- Screen time
- Study hours
- Skill development
- Commitments
- Personal goals

Every important resource deserves attention.

supporting.text: Ponder the path of thy feet, and let all thy ways be established.
So teach us to number our days, that we may apply our hearts unto wisdom.

9.illustration:
Your phone can show how much data or battery each application consumes.

Without checking the report, you may blame the wrong app.

In the same way, a money record reveals which habits are consuming your resources.
9.challenge:
Track every amount you receive and spend for seven days.

Use these headings:

- Date
- Amount Received
- Amount Spent
- Purpose
- Need or Want
- Balance
9.prayer:
Lord, give me discipline to measure what You place in my hands. Help me face my habits
honestly and make wise corrections. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
9.declaration:
I measure what I manage.
I improve what I measure.
9.transition: Once you know what you have, the next step is to give every amount an assignment.

10.title: PLAN BEFORE YOU SPEND

scripture.text: For which of you, intending to build a tower, sitteth not down first, and counteth the cost, whether he have sufficient to finish it?

10.truth: A budget is a plan that gives money an assignment before emotions spend it.

points.title: Planning Is Biblical
points.body:
Jesus used the picture of a builder who first counted the cost.

Planning is not a lack of faith.

Wise planning helps you:

- Understand what is required
- Set priorities
- Prepare for future needs
- Avoid unnecessary debt
- Complete what you begin

points.title: A Budget Protects Priorities
points.body:
Without a budget, the loudest desire may take all the money.

A simple teenage budget can include:

- Give
- Save
- Spend
- Invest
- Learn
- Help

A budget ensures that important things are not ignored.

points.title: A Budget Gives You Freedom
points.body:
Some people think a budget is a punishment.

A good budget actually gives you permission to spend within agreed limits.

It protects you from:

- Regret
- Impulse
- Peer pressure
- Confusion
- Constant shortage

supporting.text: The thoughts of the diligent tend only to plenteousness; but of every one that is hasty only to want.
There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.

10.illustration:
A football team does not enter a match with every player running wherever he feels like
running.

The team uses a formation.

A budget is a financial formation. It puts every part of your money in the right position.
10.challenge:
Create a budget for your next allowance, gift or income.

Use percentages or actual amounts under these headings:

- Giving
- Saving
- Spending
- Investing
- Learning
10.prayer:
Father, give me wisdom to plan before I spend. Help me control impulses and direct my
resources towards worthwhile purposes. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
10.declaration: I will direct my money before it disappears.
10.transition: Faithfulness is also revealed by how we treat what belongs to another person.

11.title: FAITHFUL WITH ANOTHER PERSON’S

scripture.text: And if ye have not been faithful in that which is another man’s, who shall give you that which is your own?

11.truth:
How you treat what belongs to others reveals whether you are ready for greater personal
responsibility.

points.title: Borrowed Things Are a Test
points.body:
When you borrow something, you should:

- Ask permission
- Use it carefully
- Return it promptly
- Return it in good condition
- Report any damage honestly

Carelessness with borrowed property reveals poor stewardship.

points.title: Shared Resources Also Belong to Someone
points.body:
School, family and church property may feel as though they belong to nobody.

But they belong to a community.

Examples include:

- Chairs
- Books
- Toilets
- Computers
- Sports equipment
- Musical instruments
- Electricity
- Water

Responsible people protect shared resources.

points.title: Trust Opens Doors
points.body:
People entrust greater opportunities to those who have demonstrated responsibility.

If you are faithful with:

- Someone else’s time
- Someone else’s money
- Someone else’s idea
- Someone else’s equipment
- Someone else’s confidence

You become a person who can be trusted with more.

supporting.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

11.illustration:
Two students borrow cameras.

The first student returns the camera clean, fully charged and safely packed.

The second returns it late with a missing cover and a scratched lens.

Which student will be trusted with the more expensive camera next time?
11.challenge:
Do one of the following today:

- Return something you borrowed.
- Repair something you damaged.
- Replace something you lost.
- Clean a shared space.
- Ask forgiveness for careless handling.
11.prayer:
Father, make me trustworthy with what belongs to others. Help me protect every resource
placed in my care. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
11.declaration: I honour God by caring for what belongs to another.
11.transition: Faithfulness is not only about careful handling. It is also about integrity.

12.title: CHARACTER BEFORE CASH

scripture.text: If therefore ye have not been faithful in the unrighteous mammon, who will commit to your trust the true riches?

12.truth: Money tests character. Integrity must be stronger than the desire for quick profit.

points.title: Money Reveals the Heart
points.body:
Money can reveal:

- Greed
- Fear
- Dishonesty
- Pride
- Generosity
- Contentment
- Self-control

Money does not always create character problems. It often exposes what was already present.

points.title: Integrity Is More Valuable Than Profit
points.body:
Never exchange your character for:

- Extra change
- Examination malpractice
- Internet fraud
- Stolen property
- False advertising
- Secret commissions
- Dishonest business

Money gained through corruption carries a cost greater than its value.

points.title: True Riches Require Trust
points.body:
Jesus spoke of “true riches.”

God values things money cannot purchase:

- Wisdom
- Integrity
- Spiritual understanding
- Trust
- Good character
- Kingdom responsibility

Financial faithfulness can prepare us to carry these greater treasures.

supporting.text: He that walketh uprightly walketh surely: but he that perverteth his ways shall be known.
Better is the poor that walketh in his uprightness, than he that is perverse in his ways, though he be rich.

12.illustration:
A cashier mistakenly gives a teenager ₦5,000 more than the correct change.

Nobody else notices.

Returning the money shows that the teenager’s integrity is worth more than temporary gain.
12.challenge:
Examine your recent financial actions.

Correct any dishonest act involving:

- Change
- Borrowing
- Selling
- School payments
- Online transactions
- Shared money
12.prayer:
Lord, build my character before increasing my cash. Give me courage to remain honest even
when dishonesty appears profitable. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
12.declaration: I will never exchange integrity for income.
12.transition: Faithfulness is not one good action. It is a consistent pattern.

13.title: THE FAITHFULNESS TEST

scripture.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.

13.truth: God examines how we handle little before entrusting greater responsibility.

points.title: Faithfulness Is Consistent
points.body:
Faithfulness means doing what is right:

- Repeatedly
- Quietly
- Correctly
- Promptly
- Honestly

It is not one impressive action followed by weeks of carelessness.

points.title: Faithfulness Requires Systems
points.body:
Good intentions are not always enough.

Simple systems help you become faithful:

- Keep records
- Use a budget
- Save automatically
- Return borrowed items
- Set reminders
- Review spending
- Ask for accountability

Systems make responsible behaviour easier to repeat.

points.title: Faithfulness Prepares You for Increase
points.body:
The goal is not merely to receive more money.

Faithfulness prepares you for:

- Greater trust
- Greater influence
- Greater opportunities
- Greater responsibility
- Greater impact

God’s promotion is larger than financial increase.

supporting.text: And let us not be weary in well doing: for in due season we shall reap, if we faint not.
A faithful man shall abound with blessings: but he that maketh haste to be rich shall not be innocent.

13.illustration:
Brushing your teeth for one hour once a month cannot replace brushing for a few minutes
every day.

Many results come through consistency, not occasional intensity.
13.challenge:
Create your four-part Faithfulness System:

- What will I record?
- What will I save?
- What will I stop wasting?
- Who will hold me accountable?
13.prayer:
Father, make me faithful in little. Give me discipline, honesty and consistency. Prepare my
character for every increase You desire to place in my hands. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

14.title: TWO MASTERS

scripture.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

14.truth: Jesus Christ must remain the only Master of our hearts. Money must remain a servant.

points.title: A Master Demands Loyalty
points.body:
A master has the right to command.

If money is your master, it will command you to:

- Chase it at any cost
- Compromise your values
- Compare yourself with others
- Fear constantly
- Ignore people
- Disobey God

Jesus deserves complete loyalty.

points.title: Mammon Is More Than Currency
points.body:
Mammon represents the power, confidence and identity people attach to money.

Money becomes mammon when you believe:

- Money is your ultimate security.
- Money determines your value.
- Money can solve every problem.
- Life has no meaning without wealth.
- God’s instructions can be ignored for profit.

points.title: You Must Choose
points.body:
Jesus did not present serving God and mammon as a comfortable partnership.

One must remain above the other.

The Christian order is:

- Christ is Master.
- I am His steward.
- Money is my servant.

supporting.text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
But seek ye first the kingdom of God, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you.

14.illustration:
Two people cannot safely hold and turn the steering wheel of the same moving car in opposite
directions.

There must be one recognised driver.

There must also be one recognised Master in your life.
14.challenge:
Complete this sentence honestly:

“Money most often tries to control me through __________.”

Then write one biblical response to that pressure.
14.prayer:
Jesus Christ, remain the only Master of my heart. Deliver me from every form of loyalty to
mammon. Let money remain beneath Your authority. Amen.
14.declaration: Jesus Christ alone is my Master.
14.transition: Money becomes dangerous when it takes the place that belongs to God.

15.title: GOLD IS NOT MY GOD

scripture.text: For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.

15.truth: Money itself is not evil, but loving money can corrupt faith, character and relationships.

points.title: The Bible Condemns the Love of Money
points.body:
The verse does not say that money is the root of all evil.

It warns against the love of money.

The love of money appears when people:

- Crave wealth above righteousness
- Measure everyone by possessions
- Use people to gain profit
- Refuse contentment
- Abandon faith for financial advantage

points.title: Money Makes a Poor God
points.body:
Money cannot:

- Forgive sin
- Give eternal life
- Heal every disease
- Guarantee peace
- Create genuine love
- Replace family
- Satisfy the soul

Money can solve financial problems, but it cannot carry the weight of worship.

points.title: Enjoy Resources Without Worshipping Them
points.body:
God may bless people with resources.

The correct response is to:

- Give thanks
- Remain humble
- Share generously
- Use wisely
- Refuse pride
- Maintain devotion to Christ

supporting.text: Trust not in oppression, and become not vain in robbery: if riches increase, set not your heart upon them.
Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

15.illustration:
Fire is valuable when it remains in a fireplace or cooker.

It can provide warmth and prepare food.

But when fire takes over the house, it destroys what it was meant to serve.

Money must remain in its proper place.
15.challenge:
List three things money cannot give you.

Then list three ways money can be used responsibly.
15.prayer:
Father, cleanse my heart from the love of money. Help me enjoy Your provision without
worshipping possessions. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
15.declaration:
Gold is not my god.
Jesus Christ is my Lord.
15.transition: Money can also control us through the possessions we use to define ourselves.

16.title: POSSESSIONS MUST NOT POSSESS ME

scripture.text: And he was sad at that saying, and went away grieved: for he had great possessions.

16.truth: Possessions become dangerous when they control our identity, confidence and obedience.

points.title: The Rich Young Ruler Owned Much
points.body:
The young man had many possessions.

His wealth was not the only problem.

The deeper issue was that he could not release what stood between him and obedience to
Jesus.

What he owned had gained control over his heart.

points.title: Identity Must Come From Christ
points.body:
Teenagers may be tempted to build identity around:

- Phones
- Shoes
- Clothes
- Cars
- Schools
- Neighbourhoods
- Social media appearance

These things can be enjoyed, but they must never determine personal worth.

points.title: Attachment Is Revealed by Release
points.body:
You may not know how attached you are to something until you are asked to:

- Share it
- Give it
- Delay it
- Lose it
- Live without it
- Choose obedience over it

A steward can release possessions because identity and security are found in God.

supporting.text: For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
And he said unto them, Take heed, and beware of covetousness: for a man’s life consisteth not in the abundance of the things which he possesseth.

16.illustration:
A teenager feels confident only when wearing a particular brand of shoe.

Without it, the teenager feels inferior.

The shoe is no longer merely being worn. It has started controlling the teenager’s sense of
worth.
16.challenge:
Choose one possession you value highly.

Write:

- Why do I value it?
- How would I feel without it?
- Does it affect how I see myself?
- Could I share or release it if God required it?
16.prayer:
Father, let my identity remain rooted in Christ. Deliver me from allowing possessions,
brands or appearances to control my confidence. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
16.declaration:
I possess things.
Things do not possess me.
16.transition: One of the strongest forces behind unnecessary spending is pressure.

17.title: NEEDS, WANTS AND PRESSURE

scripture.text: Not that I speak in respect of want: for I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content.

17.truth: Contentment gives us the strength to separate genuine needs from wants created by pressure.

points.title: Needs and Wants Are Different
points.body:
A need is something necessary for health, safety, responsibility or basic functioning.

A want is something desirable but not essential.

A want is not automatically wrong, but calling every want a need creates poor financial
decisions.

points.title: Pressure Can Distort Desire
points.body:
Pressure may come from:

- Friends
- Advertisements
- Influencers
- Trends
- Fear of missing out
- Comparison
- The desire to impress

Pressure can turn a useful desire into an emotional emergency.

points.title: Contentment Is Learned
points.body:
Paul said, “I have learned.”

Contentment does not mean:

- Refusing to grow
- Rejecting improvement
- Avoiding ambition
- Remaining careless

Contentment means you can be grateful and peaceful while working responsibly for
improvement.

supporting.text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
Let your conversation be without covetousness; and be content with such things as ye have: for he hath said, I will never leave thee, nor forsake thee.

17.illustration:
A teenager has a phone that performs every necessary function.

After seeing friends with newer phones, the teenager begins to feel that the present phone
is useless.

The device did not suddenly stop working. Comparison changed the teenager’s feelings.
17.challenge:
For every purchase you consider today, classify it as:

- Need
- Useful want
- Pressure-driven want

Delay any pressure-driven purchase for at least seven days.
17.prayer:
Lord, teach me contentment. Help me resist comparison and emotional spending. Give me wisdom
to recognise needs, wants and pressure. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
17.declaration:
I will not spend to impress people.
My identity is secure in Christ.
17.transition: Money stops controlling us when we deliberately give it a godly assignment.

18.title: GIVE MONEY AN ASSIGNMENT

scripture.text: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

18.truth:
Money becomes a servant when it is deliberately directed towards meaningful and eternal
purposes.

points.title: Money Is a Tool
points.body:
A tool cannot decide what it will build.

The person holding the tool gives it direction.

Money can be directed to:

- Feed
- Educate
- Build
- Support
- Create
- Invest
- Give
- Solve

Money should receive instructions from a wise steward.

points.title: Earning Should Lead to Impact
points.body:
The goal of work is not only personal consumption.

Biblical earning can provide resources to:

- Meet personal responsibilities
- Help family
- Give to others
- Support Kingdom work
- Build solutions
- Create jobs
- Develop skills

Income should become impact.

points.title: Give Before Money Controls You
points.body:
Generosity breaks the illusion that money must be held at all costs.

Giving reminds the heart:

- God is my Source.
- Money is not my security.
- People matter.
- I can release resources.
- I am a steward, not an owner.

supporting.text: Let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour, working with his hands the thing which is good, that he may have to give to him that needeth.
He that hath pity upon the poor lendeth unto the LORD; and that which he hath given will he pay him again.

18.illustration:
A teenager uses part of a holiday income to purchase books for a younger student who cannot
afford them.

The money is no longer merely currency. It has become an instrument of education and hope.
18.challenge:
Give part of your money, time or skill to meet one genuine need today.

Do it quietly and intentionally.
18.prayer:
Father, teach me to give money a godly assignment. Let my resources solve problems, build
people and advance Your purposes. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
18.declaration: My money must serve God’s mission.
18.transition:
Tomorrow, we will identify and break the chains through which mammon tries to control the
heart.

19.title: BREAK MAMMON’S CHAINS

scripture.text: No servant can serve two masters: for either he will hate the one, and love the other; or else he will hold to the one, and despise the other. Ye cannot serve God and mammon.

19.truth:
Financial freedom begins when Jesus Christ is Master and money is deliberately kept in the
position of a servant.

points.title: Mammon Chains Through Disobedience
points.body:
Money is becoming a master when you are willing to:

- Lie for it
- Cheat for it
- Steal for it
- Abandon worship for it
- Betray trust for it
- Hurt people for it

No amount of money is worth losing obedience to Christ.

points.title: Mammon Chains Through Identity
points.body:
Money is becoming a master when your confidence rises and falls according to:

- Your possessions
- Your family’s status
- Your clothes
- Your phone
- Your ability to impress people

Your identity must be anchored in Christ.

points.title: Mammon Chains Through Fear
points.body:
Money may control people by making them constantly afraid of:

- Not having enough
- Losing what they possess
- Being seen as poor
- Missing an opportunity
- Helping others
- Trusting God

Wise planning is good. Constant financial fear is another form of bondage.

supporting.text: Therefore take no thought, saying, What shall we eat? or, What shall we drink? or, Wherewithal shall we be clothed?
He that trusteth in his riches shall fall: but the righteous shall flourish as a branch.

19.illustration:
A prisoner may be connected to a chain made of gold.

The chain may look expensive, but it is still a chain.

Wealth, possessions and status can appear attractive while still keeping a heart in bondage.
19.challenge:
Practise one act of financial freedom:

- Give something.
- Delay a purchase.
- Reject peer pressure.
- Admit a dishonest action.
- Help someone.
- Save instead of showing off.
- Thank God for what you already possess.
19.prayer:
Jesus Christ, break every chain of mammon in my heart. Deliver me from greed, fear,
comparison and material pride. Remain my Master, and teach me to direct money as Your
steward. Amen.

20.title: OCCUPY UNTIL HE COMES

scripture.text: And he called his ten servants, and delivered them ten pounds, and said unto them, Occupy till I come.

20.truth:
Jesus expects His servants to remain spiritually faithful and productively engaged until He
returns.

points.title: Occupy Means Engage Productively
points.body:
The servants were not told to sit beside the money and wait.

They were instructed to put it to work.

Christian faith should produce:

- Diligence
- Creativity
- Responsibility
- Service
- Enterprise
- Productivity

Waiting for Christ is not an excuse for laziness.

points.title: Work Can Honour God
points.body:
Work is not merely a way to receive money.

Work can:

- Serve people
- Develop character
- Create solutions
- Build communities
- Express excellence
- Honour God

Productive work is part of stewardship.

points.title: Prayer and Action Belong Together
points.body:
Prayer is essential, but prayer should lead us into obedient action.

We should:

- Pray for wisdom.
- Plan carefully.
- Learn diligently.
- Work honestly.
- Review results.
- Improve continuously.

supporting.text: Whatsoever thy hand findeth to do, do it with thy might; for there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge, nor wisdom, in the grave, whither thou goest.
And whatsoever ye do, do it heartily, as to the Lord, and not unto men.

20.illustration:
A farmer cannot pray over an empty field and expect a harvest without planting seed.

Prayer invites God’s wisdom and help. Work puts that wisdom into action.
20.challenge: Spend at least thirty minutes developing a productive skill today.
20.prayer:
Lord, make me productive while I wait for Your return. Deliver me from laziness and teach me
to work heartily as unto You. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
20.declaration: I will pray, plan, work and produce.
20.transition: The greatest enemy of multiplication is burying what God has given.

21.title: DO NOT BURY IT

scripture.text: And another came, saying, Lord, behold, here is thy pound, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.

21.truth:
God does not give us gifts merely to preserve them. He expects us to develop and deploy
them.

points.title: Preservation Is Not Always Faithfulness
points.body:
The servant returned exactly what he received.

Nothing was stolen, but nothing was multiplied.

He protected the resource from loss but also prevented it from producing value.

Playing safe can become disobedience when God has instructed us to act.

points.title: Fear Buries Gifts
points.body:
People may hide their abilities because they fear:

- Failure
- Criticism
- Embarrassment
- Comparison
- Rejection
- Imperfection

Fear may keep a gift safe, but it also keeps the gift unproductive.

points.title: Gifts Grow Through Use
points.body:
A gift develops when you:

- Practise
- Learn
- Receive correction
- Attempt difficult tasks
- Serve others
- Repeat consistently

Unused ability remains undeveloped potential.

supporting.text: Wherefore I put thee in remembrance that thou stir up the gift of God, which is in thee by the putting on of my hands.
A man’s gift maketh room for him, and bringeth him before great men.

21.illustration:
A musical instrument may be beautifully designed and extremely expensive.

But if it remains permanently inside its case, it produces no music.

Your gifts must come out of hiding.
21.challenge:
Choose one gift or skill you have neglected.

Practise it for at least thirty minutes and share the result with a trusted person.
21.prayer:
Father, deliver me from fear. Help me stir up, develop and deploy every gift You have placed
within me. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
21.declaration: I will not bury what God expects me to build.
21.transition: A gift becomes increasingly valuable when it is intentionally developed.

22.title: DEVELOP YOUR GIFT

scripture.text: Seest thou a man diligent in his business? he shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before mean men.

22.truth: Natural ability becomes valuable through diligence, training and consistent improvement.

points.title: Potential Is Only a Beginning
points.body:
Potential means you could become good at something.

It does not mean you have already developed mastery.

Potential must be followed by:

- Practice
- Study
- Discipline
- Feedback
- Experience
- Improvement

points.title: Diligence Creates Distinction
points.body:
Diligence means giving careful, consistent effort.

Diligent teenagers:

- Arrive prepared
- Practise basics
- Ask questions
- Correct mistakes
- Meet deadlines
- Continue learning

Excellence is often the accumulated result of small acts of diligence.

points.title: Skill Creates Opportunity
points.body:
People are often willing to pay for:

- Useful knowledge
- Reliable service
- Creative ability
- Technical skill
- Clear communication
- Problem-solving capacity

Developing a gift can create opportunities for service, influence and income.

supporting.text: Then this Daniel was preferred above the presidents and princes, because an excellent spirit was in him; and the king thought to set him over the whole realm.
Meditate upon these things; give thyself wholly to them; that thy profiting may appear to all.

22.illustration:
A naturally talented footballer may initially perform better than others.

But if the talented player refuses training while another player practises daily, the
disciplined player may eventually become far better.

Talent gives a beginning. Diligence produces growth.
22.challenge:
Create a seven-day development plan for one skill.

Include:

- What you will practise
- How long you will practise
- What resource you will study
- Who will give feedback
- What result you hope to produce
22.prayer:
Lord, give me diligence. Help me develop every ability You have placed within me and use it
with excellence. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
22.declaration: I will practise until my gift produces value.
22.transition: Developed gifts become especially valuable when they solve real problems.

23.title: SOLVE A PROBLEM

scripture.text: And Pharaoh said unto Joseph, Forasmuch as God hath shewed thee all this, there is none so discreet and wise as thou art.

23.truth: Value is created when wisdom, skills and resources are used to solve genuine problems.

points.title: Joseph Saw More Than a Crisis
points.body:
Egypt faced a future famine.

Joseph did not merely identify the problem. He presented:

- A plan
- A system
- A storage strategy
- A leadership structure
- A long-term solution

His ability to solve the problem created opportunity and influence.

points.title: Problems Can Become Opportunities to Serve
points.body:
Around you, people may struggle with:

- Difficult school subjects
- Technology
- Transportation
- Organisation
- Cleaning
- Design
- Communication
- Access to useful information

A steward asks, “What can I do to help?”

points.title: Income Often Follows Value
points.body:
People normally exchange money for something they value.

That value may be:

- A product
- A service
- Convenience
- Knowledge
- Entertainment
- Safety
- Time saved
- A problem solved

Do not only ask, “How can I make money?”

Also ask, “What valuable problem can I solve?”

supporting.text: Look not every man on his own things, but every man also on the things of others.
When it goeth well with the righteous, the city rejoiceth: and when the wicked perish, there is shouting.

23.illustration:
A student notices that younger children struggle with mathematics.

The student organises simple revision lessons, prepares worksheets and helps the children
improve.

Knowledge has become a solution. The solution may also become a source of responsible
income.
23.challenge:
Write down three problems around you.

For each problem, answer:

- Who experiences it?
- What causes it?
- What skill could help?
- What small solution can I test?
23.prayer:
Father, give me eyes to see needs and wisdom to create solutions. Let my gifts become
valuable to my generation. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
23.declaration: I create value by solving problems.
23.transition: A wise steward does not consume every result. Part must be preserved and multiplied.

24.title: MULTIPLY, DON’T CONSUME EVERYTHING

scripture.text: Then came the first, saying, Lord, thy pound hath gained ten pounds.

24.truth:
A steward preserves and multiplies part of today’s resources instead of consuming everything
immediately.

points.title: Consumption Uses Resources Today
points.body:
Consumption is necessary.

We must spend on:

- Food
- Clothing
- Transport
- Education
- Responsibilities
- Appropriate enjoyment

The problem begins when everything is consumed and nothing is preserved.

points.title: Saving Preserves Resources
points.body:
Saving means setting aside part of today’s income for future use.

Saving can prepare you for:

- Emergencies
- Education
- Business tools
- Opportunities
- Future purchases
- Investments
- Giving

Saving gives your future self resources.

points.title: Investment Seeks Responsible Growth
points.body:
Investment places resources into something that may produce future value.

Teenagers can begin by investing in:

- Books
- Courses
- Skills
- Tools
- Small projects
- Productive equipment
- Carefully supervised financial instruments

Investment should involve learning, patience and wise guidance.

supporting.text: Wealth gotten by vanity shall be diminished: but he that gathereth by labour shall increase.
Go to the ant, thou sluggard; consider her ways, and be wise:

24.illustration:
Two teenagers receive the same holiday income.

The first spends everything on entertainment and fashion.

The second enjoys some, saves some and buys tools to begin a simple service.

They started equally, but their stewardship created different futures.
24.challenge:
For your next income, create a multiplication allocation:

- Give
- Save
- Spend
- Invest
- Learn

Set aside the saving and investment portions before spending.
24.prayer:
Father, deliver me from consuming everything. Give me wisdom to save, invest and multiply
responsibly. In Jesus’ name. Amen.
24.declaration: I am a creator and multiplier, not merely a consumer.
24.transition: The highest purpose of multiplication is not personal accumulation. It is eternal impact.

25.title: INVEST FOR ETERNITY

scripture.text: And I say unto you, Make to yourselves friends of the mammon of unrighteousness; that, when ye fail, they may receive you into everlasting habitations.

25.truth: Temporary resources should be used in ways that produce lasting and eternal impact.

points.title: Money Is Temporary
points.body:
Money can:

- Be spent
- Be lost
- Lose value
- Be stolen
- Become outdated
- Remain behind when life ends

Because money is temporary, it should be directed towards things of lasting value.

points.title: People Have Eternal Value
points.body:
Using resources to build people can produce long-term impact.

You can invest in people through:

- Education
- Mentoring
- Encouragement
- Food
- Training
- Gospel outreach
- Medical care
- Community development

The greatest return is not always measured in money.

points.title: Kingdom Investment Sends Treasure Ahead
points.body:
Jesus taught us to lay up treasure in heaven.

Kingdom investment includes:

- Supporting the gospel
- Helping the vulnerable
- Serving people
- Giving generously
- Using gifts for God’s glory
- Building lives
- Obeying God with resources

These investments produce rewards that outlive earthly possessions.

supporting.text: Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:
While we look not at the things which are seen, but at the things which are not seen: for the things which are seen are temporal; but the things which are not seen are eternal.

25.illustration:
An expensive outfit may look impressive for a season, but it will eventually wear out or
become unfashionable.

The same amount invested in a child’s education, spiritual growth or useful skill may
influence an entire lifetime.
25.challenge:
Create your Personal Multiplication Plan:

- One gift I will develop
- One problem I will solve
- One amount I will save
- One investment I will study
- One person I will help
- One Kingdom project I will support
25.prayer:
Father, teach me to use temporary resources for eternal purposes. Help me develop, multiply
and deploy everything You place in my hands for Your glory. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

26.title: THE FAITHFUL STEWARD

scripture.text: His lord said unto him, Well done, thou good and faithful servant: thou hast been faithful over a few things, I will make thee ruler over many things: enter thou into the joy of thy lord.

26.truth:
The final goal of stewardship is to hear Jesus Christ say, “Well done, good and faithful
servant.”

points.title: The Faithful Steward Recognises Ownership
points.body:
The faithful steward understands:

- God owns everything.
- God is the Source.
- Every resource carries an assignment.
- Access is not absolute ownership.
- Every steward will give an account.

This understanding produces humility and responsibility.

points.title: The Faithful Steward Manages and Multiplies
points.body:
The faithful steward:

- Records resources
- Plans before spending
- Remains honest
- Protects what belongs to others
- Develops gifts
- Solves problems
- Saves consistently
- Invests wisely
- Produces value

Faithfulness is active, not passive.

points.title: The Faithful Steward Serves Christ
points.body:
The greatest test is not how much money you possess.

It is whether Jesus Christ remains your Master.

A faithful steward can possess wealth without being possessed by wealth.

The order remains:

- Christ is my Master.
- I am His steward.
- Money is my servant.
- People are more valuable than possessions.
- Eternity guides my decisions.

supporting.text: He that is faithful in that which is least is faithful also in much: and he that is unjust in the least is unjust also in much.
And he said unto him, Well, thou good servant: because thou hast been faithful in a very little, have thou authority over ten cities.

26.illustration:
A servant may carry the king’s treasure.

The treasure may pass through the servant’s hands, but the servant must never mistake
himself for the king.

Wealth may pass through your hands, but it must never sit on the throne of your heart.
26.challenge:
Write and sign the Stewardship Covenant below.

Add:

- Your full name
- The date
- One financial habit you will begin
- One wasteful habit you will stop
- One skill you will develop
- One person or cause you will support

## FINAL STEWARDSHIP COVENANT

> Everything I am and everything I possess belongs to God.
> I am not the ultimate owner. I am His steward.
> I will manage faithfully, spend wisely, save consistently, give generously and multiply responsibly.
> I will not serve money or build my identity around possessions.
> I will use my gifts, time, knowledge, opportunities and resources to solve problems, build people and glorify God.
> I will remain faithful in little while preparing responsibly for much.
> I will use temporary resources to produce eternal impact.
> Jesus Christ will remain my Master, and money will remain my servant.

0.title: Series Opening: Whose Money Is It?
0.recap:
Yesterday we cracked open the month: **everyone serves a master**, and money is either a
useful servant or a cruel god (Ep 1). Tomorrow we begin **THE OWNERSHIP CODE** — *God owns
it; I manage it.* This week's question: *Whose money, time, talents and opportunities am I
managing?*
0.reading:
Read **Luke 16:1–13** — the parable of the shrewd manager, our anchor text for the whole
month.

*As you read, look for:* the word **steward**. Notice the manager never owned anything. He
was accused of wasting what belonged to someone else — and he still had to give an account.
questions: Jesus said you cannot serve God and mammon. Where in ordinary life does money quietly
The manager was fired for *wasting*, not stealing. What's the difference — and does that
If God owns everything in your room right now, what would you handle differently
0.prayer:
Father, before we learn how to manage money, settle the question of ownership in our hearts.
You are the Owner; we are Your stewards. Let Jesus Christ be our only Master and let money
stay our servant. In Jesus' name. Amen.
0.declaration:
Christ my Master!
Money my servant!

1.title: Week 1 Recap: THE OWNERSHIP CODE
1.recap:
**THE OWNERSHIP CODE — God owns it; I manage it.** We met **the Owner**: the earth, the
silver and the gold are all His (Ep 2). We learned who we are — **the steward**, a manager
of someone else's goods (Ep 3). We traced every ability and opportunity back to **the
Source** (Ep 4). We discovered that every resource carries an **assignment** (Ep 5), and
that one day every steward gives **an account** (Ep 6). Yesterday you signed the **Ownership
Covenant** and built your Personal Resource Inventory.
1.reading:
Read **Psalm 24:1–2**, then **Luke 16:1–2** together.

*As you read, look for:* the two halves of the code. Psalm 24 says who owns it. Luke 16 says
what the owner eventually asks for — *"Give an account of thy stewardship."*
questions: What was the hardest item on your Resource Inventory to hand back and call God's?
